discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of single microwave photons to superconducting artificial atoms
subfield: Condensed matter / quantum optics (superconducting quantum circuits)
motivation: In 2004 Blais proposed, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf with colleagues demonstrated, that a superconducting qubit coupled to an on-chip microwave resonator reaches the strong-coupling regime of cavity QED with single photons. Circuit QED turned atomic-physics concepts into engineered electrical circuits: coupling strengths far beyond those of natural atoms, photon-number-resolved spectroscopy, on-chip generation and detection of single microwave photons, and later the ultrastrong-coupling regime. Crucially, dispersive readout and resonator-mediated coupling became the architecture of essentially every superconducting quantum processor worldwide, as well as of quantum-limited amplification and microwave quantum communication. Building on the 2025 recognition of macroscopic quantum effects in Josephson circuits, this work established the light-matter interface that made those circuits a controllable quantum platform. It is a clean, reproducible, and technologically transformative discovery that opened an entirely new field of physics.
